text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's public budget deficit in 1996 may drop below 2.5 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) from the 2.8 percent envisaged by the budget act, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said.
- In October and November Poland's consumer climate improved as Poles were buying more household durables, a recent survey by the Demoskop polling institute said.

- Poland's Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH) will participate in an international banking consortium headed by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and including two other banks to finance construction of six big supermarkets on the outskirts of Moscow. Russia's Alfa Group will get a $59.5 million investment credit from the consortium.
- Canada's Saskatchewan Wheat Pool will invest $8 million in the Europort grain reloading terminal based in the Gdansk port and get a 10 percent stake in the company.

- The listed Mostostal Zabrze construction firm and the Sosnowiec-based Foster Wheeler Energy Fakop boiler maker have signed a cooperation agreement to provide their customers with complex construction offers.

- The Potworowski Kinast Grant Thornton monitoring agency is conducting a survey of Poland's small and medium-size firms within the European Business Survey Programme sponsored by the EU. Results will be published in spring 1997.
- Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), Poland's state-owned telecom monopolist, has allowed connections between subscribers of the Era GSM and Plus GSM digital mobile phone networks.

- The Huta Katowice steel mill's deficit now amounts to 42.2 million zlotys, due to a global steel trade slump and the plant's modernisation investments this year. In 1997 the results will improve as the modernisation will be completed by then, the plant's spokesperson Renata Bytomska said.

- The Elpo garment maker's financial results forecast up to the year 2000 shows a 400 percent growth in sales revenues and a 300 percent growth in net profits, the management said. Elpo will issue up to 600,000 C-series shares this month.
NOWA EUROPA
- More than 60 out of 509 firms planning to start operations in central Europe will open outlets in Warsaw.
- Shopkeepers in Szczecin, northwestern Poland, have formed a Siec (network) joint stock company to compete successfully with supermarket chains.
- Under a Polish Constitutional Tribunal ruling, Municipalities will resume control over high-value land previously allotted to an amateur gardeners' association.
- The Radom-based Radmor radio equipment maker will supply the Polish army with 140 million zlotys worth of hi-tech radio equipment made under licence from Thomson.
- The city of Chelm has contracted Britain's Southern Vectis bus transport company to set up the Chelmskie Linie Autobusowe city transport firm.
- Poland's coal mining sector's average wage is 200 percent higher than in other sectors of the national economy, while the industry's losses are growing at a record high pace.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's agriculture ministry has refused an enlargement of duty-free lighter tobacco import quotas from 300 to 3,000 tonnes which was sought by cigarette producers.
- HSBC Investment Services plans to take over the Lodz-based Dom Inwestycyjny Guziejewski i Albrecht brokerage house, the HSBC said.

- Caise de depot et placement du Quebec, Canada's major pension fund and the Polish American Investment Fund will create Poland's real estate fund to finance housing and commercial construction ventures.
ZYCIE
- The Szczecin-based Gryfia shipyard has completed plans to carry out a contract for Swinoujcie to build three ferries for the Baltic port city next year.
PARKIET
- In the first nine month of this year the state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank made a gross profit of 348 million zlotys, the bank said.
- The listed Budimex construction has launched court proceedings against the Swarzedz furniture maker alleging that it delayed settlement of Swarzedz's commercial papers.
- The Pekao SA bank will guarantee an issue of 130 convertible bonds, worth 100,000 zlotys each, by the Elektromontaz Export construction firm.
